slides.narr: Hello, friends! Look up — do you feel the sun on your face? That warm, bright sunshine is full of energy, and today we get to learn a kind of magic that is REAL: we can catch sunlight and turn it into electricity — the same electricity that lights a lamp or charges a phone! Let's find out how.

A solar panel looks like a big, flat, shiny blue tray. People put them on rooftops where the sun shines all day. Here's the amazing part — the panel doesn't burn anything and it doesn't make a sound. It just drinks in sunlight and quietly makes electricity. Isn't that wonderful? It's like a plant soaking up the sun, except instead of growing leaves, it grows POWER!

Let's follow the sunshine on its journey! First, the sun shines down on the panel. Next, the panel catches that light and makes electricity inside itself. Then the electricity runs down a wire — zoom! — all the way into your house. And finally it lights your lamp, spins your fan, and charges your radio. Sun, panel, wire, lights — four easy steps!

Now, here's a riddle: what does a solar panel do at night? It rests! When the sun goes to sleep, the panel sleeps too. So how do we keep the lights on after dark? With a battery — a special box that stores extra power during the sunny day, like saving a piece of your lunch to eat later. Day power, saved for night. Clever, right?

Every good thing has one little catch, and here is solar's: a panel doesn't last forever. After about as long as you've been alive — twice over! — it gets tired and stops making power. And here's the tricky part: a dead panel can't rot away in the ground like a banana peel or a leaf. If we just toss it in a pile, it sits there for a very, very long time. So the smart thing — the kind thing for our Earth — is to RECYCLE old panels, so the same materials can be used again. Clean power deserves a clean ending!

Now think about home — the Congo! We have big, beautiful, bright sunshine almost every single day. That sunshine is a treasure. With solar panels, a village far away from any power line can still have light in the school, a fan in the clinic, and a charged phone to call for help. The sun belongs to everyone, and it can bring power to everyone too.

You did it! Let's remember our big ideas: the sun shines on the panel, the panel makes clean electricity, a battery helps us at night, and when a panel gets old we RECYCLE it. You are now a little solar scientist! Are you ready? Let's take the quiz and earn your certificate!
Alright — moment of truth! Answer to earn your certificate. Take your time, think it through, and remember everything we just explored. I believe in you. Go!
